Source approval withheld: two correctness findings remain.

- **P2 — Multiline reads regress.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:179](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:179), `.+?` cannot cross a newline, but its terminating lookahead requires another read clause or end of input. `Read served domains from data source xcsh_fixture.\nExplain the result.` now returns `undefined`. The previous greedy extraction captured the first line and extracted `served domains`.

- **P2 — Typed object inspections still hide subsequent reads.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:183](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:183), `.find()` skips literal `existing object`, but accepts `existing certificate`. Reproduced: `Query the name of an existing certificate using data source xcsh_fixture to inspect existing certificate to read served domains` extracts `existing certificate`, losing `served domains`. The added multi-clause tests cover only literal `existing object`.

The repaired examples work: bounded clauses preserve the later read, and explicit `to read` works without an inline provider identity. In the supplied fixture, root `name` outranks `services.name` for “Query the name…”, while “Query the service name…” selects the nested property.

Caller-role coverage verifies that `provider_type=resources` excludes the data-source fixture and that caller-only data-source scope resolves the nested read. No filter bypass is apparent in this diff; filter implementation lies outside the four-file review scope.

An additional coverage gap: extraction accepts “Query **a name**…”, but the direct-root recognition accepts only an optional “the”. My focused probe produced equal root/nested name scores for that variant.

Reviewed only the four specified files and ran read-only, in-memory probes. The reported 149 passing tests were not rerun. This review does **not** provide benchmark qualification.

review2.text:
**Source-only review: changes requested.**

- **P2 — Last-clause precedence can discard the requested property.** At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:183](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:183), `.reverse().find(...)` accepts typed-object inspections because the exclusion recognizes `existing object`, but not `existing certificate`. Thus `Read served domains from data source xcsh_fixture to inspect existing certificate` extracts `existing certificate` instead of `served domains`. Likewise, appending that inspection to `Query the name of …` disables `queryProperty` and loses the name request. Prefer the last **property-bearing** clause, with the leading property query retained as fallback. Current tests cover an intermediate inspection followed by a final read, so they miss this regression.

The bounded clauses repair greedy consumption, including newline termination. Explicit `to read` supports caller-only scope. Root-name recognition accepts `the/a/an`, while preserving `service name` as a distinct request. Added tests cover caller-only resolution and a conflicting caller-role filter; no role-filter defect is evident within these four files.

No files changed, agents invoked, or network used. The reported 150 passes were not rerun. This is source review only, **not benchmark qualification**.

**Source review: one remaining P2 defect; approval withheld.**

At [terraform-property-ranking.ts:181](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/xcsh-4682-postmerge-qualification/packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/terraform-property-ranking.ts:181), last-clause precedence accepts any clause with non-stopword terms as property-bearing. Consequently:

- `Read served domains from data source xcsh_fixture to inspect the certificate` extracts `the certificate`, replacing `served domains`.
- `Query the name of an existing certificate using data source xcsh_fixture to inspect the certificate` also extracts `the certificate`, masking the `the name` fallback.

The trailing-inspection regressions cover only wording beginning with `existing`; they miss these equivalent object inspections.

Otherwise, the bounded extraction handles the supplied intermediate-inspection and multiline cases. Root-name recognition accepts `the/a/an`, while `service name` retains its modifier and avoids the direct-root shortcut. Added coverage checks caller-only scope and rejects a conflicting resources filter.

Reviewed only the four requested files. No edits, agents, network, or benchmark authoring. The reported 151 passes were not rerun; this assessment is source-only and provides no benchmark qualification.
